D023-D009_h001.question: Well, I'm a mess. I’ve been feeling really down lately, no energy for anything, even for driving the bus. My wife passed a few years ago, and I haven't been the same since. But then, every now and then, it’s like a switch flips. Suddenly, I’m buzzing with energy, full of ideas for new routes, how to make the kids' day better – I barely need any sleep. It feels great at the time, but then I crash. And that's when the eating starts. I’ll make a huge meal, or order a ton of takeout, and just devour it until my stomach hurts. I try to eat alone because I'm so embarrassed by how much I'm putting away. It's been like this for about six months now. The binges are a problem, sure, but what really gets me are these huge mood swings, way up then way down.
D023-D009_h001.options:
A. Specific Phobia
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Bipolar II Disorder
    D. Binge-Eating Disorder

D023-D009_h002.question: "Lately, Doctor, I just don't feel like myself. There are these times, and honestly, they've been going on for over six months now, where I just eat and eat. I’ll polish off a whole box of biscuits or a massive frozen pizza, even when I'm not hungry. I often find myself eating until I'm so stuffed it's uncomfortable, and I usually do it alone, tucked away, because I'm embarrassed by the sheer quantity I’m consuming. But then, on top of that, there are other periods—they last about four or five days, sometimes a week—where I'm a whirlwind. My mind races, I barely sleep, maybe two or three hours a night, yet I have boundless energy. I reorganize entire sections of the library, start a dozen new projects, and talk so fast my colleagues can barely keep up. I feel incredibly productive and 'up,' but it's not like a full-blown manic episode; I can still function at work, even if I'm a bit more irritable. I know something isn't right because both the eating and these energetic bursts are so different from my usual self."

    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Bipolar II Disorder
    D. Binge-Eating Disorder
